DonorDock Country of Support
DonorDock is a US-based company, and we support US-based nonprofits (or nonprofits with a US presence). To sign up for DonorDock, you must:
Be a registered 501(c)(3) (or similar tax-exempt classification) with the United States Internal Revenue Service.
Have a valid and active US bank account. Must be a deposit account (PayPal is not sufficient).
Have a US Government issued Social Security Number for a user that is responsible for the payout of online donations.

Contacts Overview
Contacts are the records where you store information for
Individuals, Households, and Organizations
in DonorDock. A contact record is the central place to view and manage donor details, including contact information, giving history, activities, notes, documents, badges, and marketing lists.
Each contact is also assigned a
Stage
based on giving history. Stages help your team understand whether someone is a prospect, an active donor, or has lapsed.
Contacts may be created manually, imported in bulk, or created automatically through connected tools.
What a Contact Record Includes
From a contact record, you can:
Add, view, and manage
Gifts, Pledges, and Activities
Add, upload, and manage
Documents
Add and manage
Notes
Add and manage
Badges and Marketing Lists
Update communication preferences such as
Do Not Solicit, Unsubscribed, and SMS Unsubscribed
Archive, reactivate, or delete contacts based on your permissions
Contacts can be created automatically if your organization uses tools such as Online Giving, Signup Forms, or integrations like GoFundMePro or Zapier.
Contact Types and Stages
Contact Types
DonorDock supports three contact types:
Individual
Household
Organization
Contact Stages
A contact can have one of three stages:
Prospect
Any contact with no recorded transactions in DonorDock
Donor
Any contact with a transaction recorded in the last 24 months
Lapsed
A contact who previously gave but has not given in the last 24 months
The lapsed timeframe is set to 24 months by default. Administrators may customize this timeframe in Organization Settings

Marketing Lists
What is a Marketing List?
Marketing Lists are a specific list of people that you want to communicate with for a particular reason. Contacts can be in multiple marketing lists at once.
Marketing Lists are static.
Contacts may be listed on a contact until they are manually removed. This is different than reports, where contacts are automatically added or removed from a report, depending on if the contact fits the filtering criteria at the moment the report is opened.

articles.title: Adding National Change of Address (NCOA) information to contacts
articles.content:
Donor Management Using NCOA
The National Change of Address system is an important tool for efficient Donor Management.
The NCOA database is a set of data that includes the permanent change-of-address records maintained by the U.S. Postal Service. Here is how it works:
Every time someone living in the U.S. moves and submits a change-of-address form to their local post office, their new addresses are recorded in the NCOA database.
The Post Office automatically checks addressed mail against this database for a predetermined period so that mail is appropriately forwarded to its recipient.
The USPS keeps change-of-address records on file for 48 months, which means that it can track address changes from the past four years and send mail to the correct address once the individual has moved.
Why is this important?
If an organization's Donor addresses are not updated, mail has the potential to become undeliverable.
When this happens, you can lose touch with your most loyal Donors.
Costs may increase, to include costs to process and resend returned mail.
DonorDock suggests
running a check quarterly, semi annually, or on an annual basis to ensure that you have the most up to date information for your contacts.
The following guide is intended to assist your organization in verifying addresses using the NCOA database. This process can be broken down into 3 easy steps:
Export the list of Donors in question from DonorDock using a Contact Report
Run this export through
National Change of Address (NCOA)
database
Import Data back into DonorDock with our easy to use Import tool

To view and manage your current custom fields:
Log in to DonorDock
Navigate to
Contacts

On the
Contacts

black settings wheel

To create a new custom field

Choose the field type you want to create:

Number

(Optional) Add a

required

To view custom field values on a Contact Record
Select
Contacts
from the Navigation bar at the top of DonorDock and select
Contacts
Once on the Contacts page, you may use the search bar to search for the contact/s in question you wish to see
Clicking on the name of the contact will open their details page
The List View dropdown may also be used to narrow down your contact list view. By default, the All Contacts view will be shown when you first navigate to the Contacts page
Once on the Contact details page, click the Show More button on the bottom of the contact overview to view all field responses for the contact. Custom fields will appear towards the bottom.
Archiving a Custom Field
If you no longer need a custom field but want to preserve the data for historical or reference purposes, you can
archive the field
. Archiving a custom field removes it from your list of active fields—freeing up one of your available slots—while keeping the existing data on each contact record intact.

Contacts

The field will not appear in forms, templates, or reports.

Key Requirements for Mapping Custom Fields

The Custom Field must already exist in DonorDock.
You cannot create a new Custom Field during the import process. All custom fields must be created beforehand by going to your Contacts page, opening the settings menu, and selecting "Custom Fields."
The values in each row under that column will be imported as the value for that field.
For instance, if you have a column labeled
Parent

True

This guide will walk you through the process of using the import feature in DonorDock to upload your data into DonorDock.
Step 1: Prepare Data
Data spreadsheets may be imported into DonorDock in .csv, .tsv, .xls, .xlsx, .xml, or .txt file formats. Data may also be entered directly on the import page using the provided pop-up spreadsheet.

Step 2: Upload File/s

Settings Menu
(grid icon top right) and select Imports
From the left, click
Upload
Turn on the toggle for
Match on Email Only?

Upload data from files

Step 3: Match columns to DonorDock Values
You will now be on the match screen, which will allow you to match your columns with DonorDock data points.
Columns automatically suggest matches using AI. If the suggested match is incorrect, you can click on the dropdown on the right to adjust the suggested DonorDock value.
💡 You no longer need to confirm mapping on each column however, you should still check that each suggested mapping is correct, and if there are any incorrect mappings, adjust before continuing

Once all columns have been reviewed, click the blue
Continue
button in the top right.
Step 3.2: Secondary Map columns

💡Example: A column on the first mapping screen was mapped to Payment Types. A secondary mapping option will be available to confirm what payment types will equal which payment types in DonorDock. Such as Wire Transfer on the spreadsheet equaling ACH in DonorDock, AMEX equaling Credit Card, etc.

Any columns that were ignored or not mapped will not appear on the spreadsheet.
Any errors detected on the spreadsheet will be highlighted in red. To view only rows that have errors, click on the red
INVALID

You may type directly on the review cells to correct or remove any data showing an error (for example, email address missing an '@' symbol). Hovering over any highlighted box will explain why an error has been detected.
Step 5: Submit your Import

Process Import
at the top right of the page.
Your import will begin shortly.
The file will show pending during the import process on the Import page.
There is no need to stay on this page during the import process.
Once complete, the system will show the totals for
Donors Added, Donors Updated, Campaigns, Funds, Appeals, Gifts Added, Gifts Updated, Activities, Notes,
and any errors that occurred. To view details on any errors, click
Show

💡 If you need to undo an import for any reason, you can select the red
UNDO
button to the right of a completed import, and all new records added during the import will be removed.

articles.title: Detecting Duplicate Contacts during Import
articles.content:
Detecting Duplicate Contacts during Import
During an import, DonorDock examines your database to determine whether the contact already exists within DonorDock. If your spreadsheet contains either the Donor ID or Account Number and corresponds to an existing contact with the same Account Number/Donor ID, the system will identify a match and update the contact record with any new or different information provided in the import.
💡 When a contact is created in DonorDock, they are automatically assigned a unique Donor ID. An example of a Donor ID format is 6d32fd61-5adb-4d04-a216-0bb0a6fbb5b3. The account number field, meanwhile, can be set to an external value from another system to assist with matching across different databases.
Including an Account Number or Donor ID in your import significantly increases the probability of finding a matching record.
If a combination of different fields indicates a match, gifts will be added to the existing record, but
no contact information
will be overwritten or updated on the existing record. To update any contact details, the contact's unique account number or Donor ID must be included in the import spreadsheet.
In
Composite Matching
, where a match is confirmed from multiple fields, different data cells in the import row are compared with your database. Each field carries its own point value. If the cumulative points from these fields reach three or more in an import row, the contact/gift will be linked to an existing record rather than creating a new contact record.
If more than one contact matches, the contact with the highest score will be used.

Tips and Tricks for matching contacts while importing
If your spreadsheet contains an Account Number or Donor ID and a blank field, the data in the contact record's field will remain unchanged. Updating contact information in an import will never selectively delete information.

If adding or matching to Organization or Household records, the field for Company/Household Name is all that is needed to confirm a match (the equivalent of 3 points), however in order to update an Organization or Household record in an import, the Donor ID or Account Number for that record is still required.

articles.title: Soft Credits Overview

Soft Credits in DonorDock

articles.title: Receipts Overview
articles.content:
Receipts Overview
Providing donors with receipts for donations is important. The donation receipt serves as documented evidence that the donor has contributed to the organization. This transparency builds trust between your non-profit and your donors as you foster a continuing relationship with them.
Donation receipts are also essential for donors who claim tax deductions for their giving. In many places, individuals and businesses can deduct their charitable contributions from their taxable income, thereby lowering their tax liabilities. To take advantage of these benefits, donors need accurate documentation of their contributions.
In DonorDock, receipts may be set to automatically send for gifts received through DonorDock Online Giving Pages. Receipts may also be sent manually on an individual basis or in bulk from reports.

articles.title: Recurring Gifts Overview
articles.content:
Recurring Gifts
This article covers recurring gifts using DonorDock, and how to track recurring gifts, import recurring gifts, make changes to recurring gifts, report on recurring gifts, and more.
Recurring gifts

articles.title: Gift Tags
articles.content:
Gift Tags Overview
What are Gift Tags?
Gift tags identifiers are tied to a gift record to characterize and segment the gift based on characteristics that are not covered by Campaign, Appeal, Fund, and Tracking Code functionality. Gift tags are a long-term tag that are stored on a gift record indefinitely.
Like Badges are for contact records, Gift tags are a simple yet versatile way for you to be able to identify and sort your gifts to meet your organization's needs.
Examples of Gift Tags that may be used for: Major Gift, Matching Gift, Silent Auction Gift, etc.

In DonorDock,

articles.title: Campaigns Overview
articles.content:
Campaign Overview
Campaigns are available in DonorDock for easy tracking designation for gifts.
A campaign set as one of the following types:
Fundraising
This campaign type may be used to cover your organization's fundraising goals that are not specifically an event or a grant.
Example: an Annual Campaign, where multiple appeals contribute to the overall campaign
Event
This campaign type may be used for a specific event, such as a gala.
Example: An event campaign for a gala with multiple appeals for contributions for the gala yet the total campaign covers the entire event.
Grant
A campaign type to help with the tracking of grant gifts and activities. Using this campaign type allows you to track all your grant related activities (tasks, asks, meetings, phone calls, and notes, as well as gifts and pledges), in one place.
💡 You may have as many Appeals associated with a Campaign as you like, however you may not link Campaigns to each other.

articles.title: Appeals Overview
articles.content:
Appeal Overview
Appeals are available for tracking DonorDock so that your organization can track the generation of gifts and how they were solicited. An appeal may be linked directly to a specific campaign, and you may have as many Appeals associated with a Campaign as you like.
Primary Promotional Channels available for Appeals
Email
Direct Mail
Event
Social Media
Phone Calls
Website
💡 Event is also available as a Campaign type so that you may have the overall campaign be specific to an event or have an appeal for the event linked to an overarching campaign.

articles.title: Funds Overview
articles.content:
Funds Overview
Funds are a helpful tool for tracking where donations are directed. They allow you to track the purpose of each donation and where the donor intended their contribution to be used. When integrated with your Accounting system, fund accounting enables more precise management of how each donation is used by your organization.
💡 If working with QuickBooks, it is important that Fund information (Naming convention, Account Number, Account Class Name, etc) matches between DonorDock and QuickBooks.

articles.title: The Differences between Campaigns, Appeals, and Funds
articles.content:
Campaigns, Appeals, and Funds
Campaigns, Appeals, and Funds are different options to allow your organization to coordinate and sort your fundraising easily.
The basic layout for tracking in DonorDock is that
Campaigns
are
what
your organization is raising donations for,
Appeals
are
how
you are raising donations, and
Funds
are
where
those donations are going.
Campaigns
are the main goals explaining what your organization is raising money for. Appeals may be directly linked to a Campaign.
💡  You may have as many Appeals associated with a Campaign as you like. However, you may not link Campaigns to each other.
Appeals
are resources that are used by your organization to track how you are soliciting donations.
💡 Appeals may be in the form of email, direct mail, events, social media, phone calls, and websites.
Funds
are an optional piece for tracking where you store information about where a donation is being directed for use.
💡 This feature is helpful if your organization does Fund accounting. Funds allow you to create Fund records within DonorDock that you can tag gifts to. This is useful if you integrate DonorDock with your Accounting system and you do Fund Account.

articles.title: Merging Campaigns, Appeals, and Funds
articles.content:
Merging Campaigns, Appeals, and Funds
Sometimes, you might find duplicate Campaigns, Appeals, or Funds in your records. To combine two campaigns/appeals/funds into one, you can utilize the merge function within the Transactions table view.
Merge Two Campaigns
Navigate to
Transactions
in the top navigation of DonorDock
Select
Campaigns
On the table of campaigns, on the left, check the boxes for the two campaigns in question
Click the
merge
action in the top right
In the confirmation box, click which campaign you would like to keep
Your merge is now completed. All donations and activities will be transferred to the designated campaign, while the campaign not retained will be archived.
Merge Two Appeals
Navigate to
Transactions
in the top navigation of DonorDock
Select
Appeals
On the table of appeal, on the left, check the boxes for the two campaigns in question
Click the
merge
action in the top right
In the confirmation box, click which appeal you would like to keep
Your merge is now completed. All donations and activities will be transferred to the designated appeal, while the appeal not retained will be archived.
Merge Two Funds
Navigate to
Transactions
in the top navigation of DonorDock
Select
Funds
On the table of funds, on the left, check the boxes for the two campaigns in question
Click the
merge
action in the top right

If you select "All" in the view dropdown to see a mix of active and archived Campaigns/Appeals/Funds, the merge option will not be accessible. This measure is in place to avoid unintentionally merging an active with an archived Campaign/Appeal/Fund.

articles.title: DAFpay with DonorDock
articles.content:
DAFpay with DonorDock
DonorDock giving pages include
DAFpay
powered by
Chariot
, the leading payments platform for charitable giving. DAFpay enables donors to make gifts directly from their Donor-Advised Funds (DAFs), providing your organization with access to funds that are already set aside for philanthropy.
💡 DAFpay is automatically enabled on your online giving pages by default using your organization’s EIN and email address, but it can be disabled at any time in your page settings.
What is a Donor-Advised Fund (DAF)?
A Donor-Advised Fund (DAF) is a type of charitable investment account designed for giving. Donors contribute to their DAF, receive an immediate tax deduction, and then recommend grants from the fund to nonprofit organizations over time. Because the money is already earmarked for charity, DAFs represent a committed source of generosity. Donors are not deciding
whether
to give; they are deciding
where
to give.
How a Donor uses DAFpay
The donor enters a
one-time donation amount
on your giving page.
The donor selects the
DAFpay button
at the bottom of the page
A pop-up window opens with a brief overview of DAFpay terms and conditions. The donor clicks
Continue
to agree
The donor searches for and selects their
DAF provider
(for example, Fidelity Charitable or Schwab Charitable)
The donor logs in to their DAF provider and submits the donation.
💡DAFpay is only available for one-time donations and cannot be used for monthly, quarterly, or yearly recurring donations.
Tracking DAFpay Gifts in DonorDock
When a donation is made through DAFpay on your DonorDock giving page, the gift is automatically recorded in DonorDock as two donations. The received donation will track to the Donor Advised Fund organization record that is paying the funds and a second, linked soft credit gift will be created on the donor record who directed the gift.
No receipt will be sent to the Donor from DonorDock as they should receive acknowledgement from their Donor Advised Funds.
Each DAFpay gift is assigned a
10-digit alphanumeric identifier
, which is stored as the
Tracking Code
in DonorDock while the Grant ID from Chariot will be entered in the
Payment ID
Field. If any issues arise, you can use this number when following up with Chariot support.
The
Payment Type
will be set to
DAFpay
, and the gift will be automatically tagged with
DAFpay Gift
to make reporting easy
The status of the gift will be in processing status and will update to received status when Chariot sends an update of a successful donation.
Otto Tips
🌊
U.S. waters only:
DAFpay can only be used by donors with a U.S. address.
🐚
Valid ship papers required:
Your organization must be a registered 501(c)(3) with a valid EIN to receive DAFpay gifts.
⚓
One-time voyages:
DAFpay works only for one-time donations. Recurring gifts (monthly, quarterly, or yearly) are not supported.
🛞
You’re the captain:
DAFpay is your choice. Keep it on to accept DAF gifts, or toggle it off anytime.

articles.title: Creating An Online Giving Page
articles.content:
Creating an Online Giving Page
New Giving Pages may be created by navigating to
Online Giving
and clicking
+Add Giving Page
at the top right of the page.
Settings for the giving page are divided into different segments for ease of access and editing:
⭐ Basics
The Basics are the foundation of the giving page, Here you may set the Name of the form, what type of gifts are being accepted through the giving page, branding elements (color, logo, and featured image), and set the main message for the page.
For best results when adding a featured image, the image should be: 1000px Wide x 465px tall or 632px x 300px.
This Canva
Featured Image Template
is also available to assist you with creating/formatting your Featured Image for the best results. This message is what your donors will see when they visit your online giving landing page. In addition to Text, you may also insert Images links using the
Picture
🖼️Icon.
⭐ Choose Amounts
The Choose Amounts section relates to the donation options for the page. Here you may set the goal for the page, elect whether the donor can see that goal and progress towards the goal, set if Donor's will cover fees by default, as well as set donation options in relation to frequencies available and custom and preset donation amounts.
⭐ Collect Information
The Collect Information settings allow you to set what type of information you collect from the Donor, in regards to allowing tribute gifts, anonymous donations, or receiving donor comments on gifts.
⭐ Success Settings
Under Success Settings, you may customize the experience of the donor after their gift has been completed. Upon successful gift, you may create and customize a message to be displayed on the giving page or redirect the donor to an URL of your choice. You may also customize the template for the thank you/receipt email the donor will receive, as well as the team member who will show as sending the thank you/receipt email.
⭐ Tracking
From the Tracking section, you may set different tracking sections to apply to gifts that are received through the giving page. Here you may set the Campaign, Appeal, Funds, Gift Tags, Badges, and Marketing Lists.
⭐ Text-to-Donate
Text-to-donate is one way to make donating to your organization easier. This feature allows your donors to text you a keyword, and receive a custom automatic response text message from you, with a link to a donate page. This keyword may be used at events, shared via email, or mail communications to make it as easy as possible to donate to your organization.
Once you have completed all the fields on the Giving Page setup you wish, click
Save
at the top of the Giving Page. Once you have saved the page, a preview of the page will appear on the right. You may continue to making changes and tweaks if necessary.
Once you are satisfied with the preview of the giving page, you may
Publish
the page in the top right.
Once published, the Sharing options for the page will appear on the left. You may also set the giving page as your default giving page if needed.

articles.title: Reporting Overview
articles.content:
Reporting Overview
Reports help you make sense of the data you are tracking in DonorDock. They enable you to analyze contacts, gifts, and activities, allowing you to understand trends and measure outcomes better.
When generating a report, you can:
Start with a
preformatted standard report
.
Create a
custom report
from scratch.
Reports can also be saved for future use. A saved report stores your chosen filters and columns, but always pulls in the latest data available at the time of generation. This ensures your reports are always up to date.
Accessing Reports
Go to the
Reporting menu
.
Click on
Reports
.
On the Reports page, you will see three columns for Contact, Gift, and Activity Reports.
Within each column, the
system standard reports
are listed first, followed by any
custom reports
you have saved.
Report Types
Contact Reports
A contact report shows one row for each unique contact. A specific contact record will only appear once in a contact report, even if it meets multiple filter criteria.
💡 By default, contact reports exclude contacts marked as
Deceased
or
Do Not Solicit
. To include these contacts, click the blue
Filters
button in the top right corner after the report has generated. Check the boxes to include
Deceased
and/or

, then run the report again to update the results.
Standard Contact Reports
Report Name
Focus

Gift Reports
A gift report shows one row for each unique gift. If a contact has made multiple gifts in the report’s time frame, their name may appear multiple times.
Some system reports summarize giving instead of listing individual gifts. For example, the

Focus

In-Kind Contribution Statements

Activity Reports
An activity report shows one row for each unique activity. If a contact has multiple activities during the report’s time frame, they will appear multiple times.
Standard Activity Reports
Report Name
Focus

Report that specifically shows contacts who clicked the unsubscribe link in a bulk email, the date they unsubscribed, current unsubscribed status, and the email they clicked the link.
Otto Tips
🌊
Pick the right type:
Choose a contact, gift, or activity report based on whether you want to count people, gifts, or actions.
🐚
Save time later:
If you run the same report often, save it so you can quickly pull updated results.
⚓
Filters matter:
Saved reports remember your filters and columns, but always refresh with the latest data.
🦑
Know the exceptions:
Some standard reports, like Giving Summary, will summarize results instead of listing every individual row.

articles.title: Reporting on DAFpay Gifts in DonorDock
articles.content:
Reporting on Donor Advised Funds (DAFs) and DAFpay Gifts in DonorDock
Reporting is a crucial aspect of understanding donor behavior and monitoring the impact of contributions. DonorDock makes it easier to report on Donor Advised Fund (DAF) donations by automatically tagging and structuring these gifts. This ensures that both the originating DAF provider and the directing donor are properly recognized and that reporting is clear and flexible.
How DAFpay Gifts Are Recorded
When a DAFpay donation is made through a DonorDock giving page, two gifts are automatically created:
Received Gift
: Created on the organization account for the Donor Advised Fund that processed the donation.
Linked Soft Credit Gift
: Created on the individual donor’s contact record to recognize the donor who directed the gift.
Automatic Tagging and Badges
Specific Badge and Gift Tags will apply automatically when these gifts are created in DonorDock.
The DAF provider organization is tagged with the badge
Chariot DAF Provider
.
The
received gift
is tagged with
DAFpay Gift
.
The
linked soft credit gift
is tagged with both:
DAFpay Soft Credit
(specific to Chariot gifts made through giving pages).
Linked Soft Credit
(the standard tag used for any soft credit linked to a parent gift).
This dual tagging enables the distinction between DAFpay soft credits generated through Chariot and other soft credits that were manually linked.
These automatic badges and tags make it simple to segment data and generate reports.
Quick Report Idea: View All DAF Providers
Open the
Contacts
menu in the navigation bar.
Select
Contact Lists
.
On the left-hand side, click the
Chariot DAF Provider
badge.
A Contact Report will load showing all DAF organizations that have provided gifts.
Quick Reporting Idea: View All DAFpay Gifts
Open the
Transactions
menu in the navigation bar.
Select
Gifts
.
Click
Manage Tags
at the top of the page.
In the tags list, click
DAFpay Gift
or
Linked Soft Credit
.
A Gift Report will load, showing all gifts with that tag.
Running Custom Reports with Multiple Gift Tags
Sometimes it is useful to view both received DAFpay gifts and their linked soft credits in one report. A custom Gift Report allows this.
Navigate to the
Reports
page under the Reporting menu.
Click the blue
+ Create
button (or the
+ Create
button at the bottom of the Gift Reports column).
Select to create a
Custom Gift Report
.
In the filter box:
Set the desired
Date Range
(e.g.,
This Year
).
On the
Tags
filter line, add both
DAFpay Gift
and
DAFpay Soft Credit
.
Click
Run Report
.
The report will now display all gifts that are tagged with either of those gift tags, allowing both received and soft credit gifts to appear in the same dataset.
Customizing Gift Report Columns
Gift Reports can be further tailored by adjusting the visible columns:
On your report, click the
Columns
icon on the right-hand side.
Add or remove columns as needed.
For DAF reporting, consider adding:
Related Soft Credits
Related Soft Credit $
These fields allow you to see, on the same row as a received gift, the amount of soft credit linked to that gift.
Otto Tips
⚓
Two ships, one journey
: Remember that every DAFpay donation creates both a received gift and a soft credit. Watch both records to see the full picture.
🧭
Chart combined waters
: Custom Gift Reports with multiple tags let you view received and soft credit gifts side by side.
🦑
Dive deeper
: Add
Related Soft Credits
and
Related Soft Credit $
to see how provider gifts and donor credits connect on one line.
🚢
Know your currents
: When creating reports, gift tags like
DAFpay Soft Credit
give you a current-specific view of Chariot transactions, while broader tags show the whole tide of linked gifts.

articles.title: Using Reports to create Mailing Lists
articles.content:
Using Reports to create Mailing Lists
When creating appeals and deciding who you will be sending marketing communications to, often you will need to sort your contacts based on their communication options.
The most frequent way to do this is to filter a report based on contacts who have an email address listed or have a physical address listed, easily identifying which contacts are able to receive an email and/or a direct mail letter.
Filter a Report to Contacts who have an Email Address:
Navigate to Reports and run a Contact report (for example the All Contacts report under Contact reports will pull Contacts).
Once the Contact report has run, click the filter icon on the Email column and select to Filter to those contacts that "IS NOT EMPTY" for the email field.
The report will now show all contacts who have an email value. You may continue to apply any other filters or add to a marketing list to use for an email communication.
Filter a Report to Contacts who have a Physical Address:
Navigate to Reports and run a Contact report (for example the All Contacts report under Contact reports will pull Contacts).
If the address fields are not yet on the report, click the columns icon to add Address fields such as Addressee, Line 1, Line 2, Line 3, State, Zip, etc.
Once the Contact report has been run and you have the appropriate columns on the report, click the filter icon next to the Address Line 1 column, and select to filter to those that "IS NOT EMPTY" for the Line 1 field.
The report will now show all contacts who have at least a Line 1 of a physical address listed. If you wish to filter further, you may add a "IS NOT EMPTY" filter on the Zip code or State columns as well if you are worried you may have incomplete addresses.
Once the report is set with your address information, you may add the contacts to a marketing list, use the letters button to create marketing letters for the contacts, or export the report to Excel or PDF.
Marketing lists are static, disposable objects that can be deleted after used for their intended purpose.

articles.title: Action Board Overview
articles.content:
Action Board Overview
The Action Board is your personal home board in DonorDock. It serves as your daily work landing page, displaying nudges, assigned actions, and tasks you are responsible for completing. This board helps you stay focused on what needs attention today and what is coming up next.
The Action Board brings together your individual work across DonorDock, including items that may also appear on Project Boards or Ask Boards. This means you can manage your personal workload in one place while still contributing to larger projects and fundraising pipelines.
How the Action Board Works
The Action Board is made up of four lanes that organize your work for the day:
❔
Nudges
System-generated suggestions to reach out to contacts based on your data and engagement history. Nudge types can be customized in your profile.
✉️
Actions
Activities and tasks assigned to you, created by you or others. This includes Tasks and Asks that may also appear on Project Boards or Ask Boards.
✅
Completed Today
Items you completed today.
⏰
Snoozed
Nudges or actions you chose to revisit later.
A counter appears in the main navigation next to the Action Board, showing how many open nudges and actions you currently have.
Steps at a Glance
Open the Action Board from the main navigation
Review nudges and assigned actions
Create or assign new actions
Complete, snooze, or ignore items
Customize filters and notifications
Full Navigation Steps
Step 1: Access the Action Board
Log in to DonorDock
Click
Actions
in the main navigation
You can open the Action Board from anywhere in DonorDock and always see the counter showing the number of open items.
Step 2: Add Items to the Action Board
Action cards can be added to the Action Board in several ways:
Drag a
Nudge
card into the Actions lane and select the activity type
Click
Add Action
on a Nudge card
Click
+ Add Action
in the top right of the Action Board
Create an incomplete activity from
Quick Add
or a contact record and toggle
Add to Action Board
Import activities with the
Add to Action Board
column set to TRUE
Actions may be created for yourself or another team member. Once created, the action appears on the owner’s Action Board and in the contact’s activity history as an incomplete activity.
Available Action Types
You can add the following activity types to the Action Board:
Send Email
Log Email
Send Text
Log Text
Phone Call
Letter
Meeting
Task
*
Ask
*
Tasks may also be assigned to a
Project Board
, and Asks may also appear on an
Ask Board
, while still showing on the Action Board for personal follow-through.
Assign Actions to Team Members
To assign an item from the Action Board:
Click the
three-dot action icon
on a card
Select
Assign
Choose a team member
You can also assign actions at the time of creation. Assigned users will see the item on their Actions Board and may receive an email notification if enabled in profile settings.
Step 3: Complete Actions
Complete from the Action Board
Method 1
Drag the card to
Completed Today
Enter completion notes
Click
Mark Complete
Method 2
Click the three-dot
action icon
on a nudge card
Select
Complete
Enter completion notes
Click
Mark Complete
Complete from the Activity Record
Open the activity record from the card
Click
Mark Complete
Add completion notes
Save
Completed actions will appear in the Completed Today lane and in the contact’s activity history.
Snooze or Ignore Items
Snooze an Item
Drag the card to
Snoozed
, or
Click the three-dot icon and select
Snooze
Choose to snooze for one day, one week, or one month
If an action has a due date before the snooze wake date, the due date is pushed to the wake date.
Wake a Snoozed Item
Click the three-dot icon on the snoozed card
Select
Wake
Ignore an Item
Click the three-dot icon
Select
Ignore
Ignoring an Action removes the card from the Action Board. The activity record remains incomplete on the contact record until it is completed. Ignoring a nudge removes it from the Action board, and the nudge will not appear anywhere else in DonorDock.
Step 4: Filter and Customize the Action Board
Filter Cards
Use filters at the top of the Action Board to filter by:
Date range
Activity type
Nudge type
Customize Nudge Preferences
Click
Customize
at the top of the Action Board
Or go to
Settings > My Profile
Set Email Notifications
Enable or disable email notifications for Action Board items in your profile settings.
Nudge Types
Nudges are system-generated suggestions to engage with contacts based on your data and engagement history. They are meant to prompt timely outreach, such as following up after a gift, reconnecting with a donor who has gone quiet, or acknowledging an important milestone.
Nudges are not actions themselves. They do not create an activity record in DonorDock until you choose to act on them. When you convert a nudge into an action, you select the activity type, such as a phone call, email, task, or Ask, and that activity is then created and tracked like any other activity in DonorDock.
Nudges only appear on the Action Board. They do not show on contact records and are not included in activity reports until they are converted into a specific activity. This keeps nudges lightweight and focused on prompting action without cluttering activity history until real work begins.
Available Nudge Types
Nudge Name
Description
Daily 5
Generated suggestions that are created by the system if you have not engaged with a donor within 30 days or more. No more than five of these daily tasks will show in the suggestions on any given day.
First Gift Anniversary
Notification on the anniversary of the Donor's first gift
Major gifts
When setting up your organization's settings, you can define what constitutes a major gift. The default value is $1000.00, but you can configure this field to align with your organization's operating practices.
Spike-up gifts
A spike-up gift is one that is out of the ordinary for a donor. For example, if a donor's average gift is $50 and they then give a $350 donation, that would be a spike. A spike-up gift is a great opportunity to reach out to a donor and learn more about what drove them to give more than they normally do. Did something change with their personal circumstances? Did something your nonprofit did resonate with them? You can set the amount above their average gift that triggers the spike-up gift notification in your Settings. The default value is $100.00
First gifts
As the name suggests, this is a nudge to engage with a donor when they give their very first gift to your nonprofit. This deserves an individual engagement activity
Second gifts
Perhaps even more important to your organization than a first gift, the second gift is significant as it moves a donor from a one-time giver to a retained donor. This is a big deal and deserves an engagement touch-point from your organization. You will receive a nudge on the ActionBoard for every second gift
Reactivated donors
Donors that have moved from an archived to an activated status
Donor moving toward inactivity
The donor has not given a gift in at least 6 months, and has not had any interaction in at least 3 months
Donor birthdays
The birthday of the Donor
Pledge payment reminders
When a donor payment for the pledged amount is due
Contacts marked as deceased are automatically excluded from nudges.
Otto Tips
🧭
Start your day here:
The Action Board is your daily command center.
⚓
Use boards together:
Tasks and Asks can live on Project Boards or Ask Boards and still show here for personal follow-through.
🌊
Snooze with intention:
Snoozing is for timing, not avoidance. Wake items when you are ready to act.
🗺️
Tune your nudges:
Customize your nudge settings so you only see suggestions that fit your role.

articles.title: Ask Board Overview
articles.content:
Ask Board Overview
The Ask Board in DonorDock helps your organization plan, manage, and track fundraising Ask activities as part of a structured moves management process. Moves management is a strategy used to guide potential donors through intentional steps, from initial identification to a completed gift, while building strong, personalized donor relationships along the way.
The Ask Board provides a visual way to organize and monitor these Asks, so your team can see progress, prioritize outreach, and coordinate efforts across donors and campaigns.
How the Ask Board Works
The Ask Board is a visual Kanban-style board with lanes that represent Ask Stages. Each Ask appears as a card that can be viewed, edited, and moved as it progresses.
Access to the Ask Board is available to users with the Administrator or User role.
Asks belong to a single Ask Board at a time and can also appear on a team member's Actions Board, ensuring visibility for both ask tracking and individual team member follow-through.
Steps at a Glance
Open the Ask Board from the Boards menu
View Asks by stage using the board lanes
Create, edit, or move Ask cards
Use filters to refine what is displayed
Track progress using Ask Board metrics
Full Navigation Steps
Step 1: Access the Ask Board
Log in to DonorDock
Click Boards in the main navigation and select Asks
Ask Board prompt in Board Menu
The Ask Board displays lanes for each Ask Stage configured for your organization.
The Ask Board displays lanes for each Ask Stage in your organization. By default, these stages are:
Identify (20%)
Qualify (30%)
Cultivate (50%)
Solicit (70%)
Close (100%)
Each percentage reflects the progression of your relationship with the donor and the likelihood of securing a commitment.
AskBoard with default system stages
Step 2: Use Ask Board Filters and Metrics
Filters
At the top of the AskBoard, you can filter by:
Board View
Select the arrow icon next to the current board name to view other board options or create a new Ask Board
Ask Board selector option menu
Ask View
Select the filter icon dropdown on the top tools to toggle between:
My Asks
and
All Asks
on the board

Date Range View
Select the Calendar dropdown to adjust the date filter by the due date range you want to view on the board
Date Filter dropdown options
Metrics
Based on your selected filters, the Ask Board displays:
Total Ask Amount
Total planned Ask amount for visible cards
Weighted Ask Amount
Total Ask value weighted by stage probability
Open Ask Amount
Total value of Asks not yet at 100%
New Ask Amount
Total value of Asks created in the last 30 days
Step 3: Create and Manage Ask Activities
Ask activities are used to track planned fundraising requests and outreach within your moves management process. Each Ask represents a specific fundraising action tied to a contact and can be updated as the relationship progresses.
You can create Ask activities from several places in DonorDock, depending on your workflow:
Ask Board
Click the Add Ask button in the top right corner of the board to create a new Ask
Add Ask button on AskBoard
Action Board
Add an Ask through the add Action on a nudge or through the Add Action option on the Action Board
Add Action button on ActionBoard

Quick Add Menu

Specific Contact Record
Open a contact’s profile and add an Ask activity tied directly to that individual
Contact Add button to Add records to Contact
Reports
Create Ask activities in bulk for multiple contacts using report-based actions
Bulk Add Menu options in Report: Badges, Marketing Lists, and Activities
Available Fields When Creating an Ask
When creating an Ask activity, you will be prompted to complete several fields that help define and track the Ask:
Field Name
Description
Contact
The individual, household, or organization that the Ask activity is assigned to
Assigned To

When to Mark an Ask as Complete
An Ask should be marked Complete once the planned fundraising action has reached a clear outcome. Completing Asks at the right time keeps your pipeline accurate and ensures reporting reflects real progress.
An Ask could be marked as completed when:
The Ask has been made
The solicitation conversation, meeting, or request has occurred, regardless of the donor’s response.
A commitment is received
The donor agrees to give, pledge, or sponsor, even if payment will occur at a later time.
The Ask is declined
A clear “no” is received, and no further solicitation is planned for this Ask.

Project Board Overview
The Project Board in DonorDock is a visual, Kanban-style board that helps teams organize, manage, and track work across projects. It allows you to group related tasks into lanes of your choosing, making it easier to see progress, coordinate efforts, and keep projects moving forward.
Project Boards are especially useful for managing multi-step initiatives such as campaigns, events, onboarding processes, or internal workflows where tasks need to be tracked over time.
How the Project Board Works
The Project Board is built around Tasks, an activity type in DonorDock used to track tasks that need to be completed or planned. Tasks appear as cards on the board and move through lanes that represent stages of work, such as To Do, In Progress, or Completed.
Tasks belong to a single Project Board at a time and can also appear on a team member's Action Board, ensuring visibility for both project tracking and individual team member follow-through.

articles.title: Board Options in DonorDock
articles.content:
Board Options in DonorDock
DonorDock includes three board types that help your team plan work, manage fundraising pipelines, and stay on top of daily actions. Each board serves a different purpose, and together they provide both big-picture visibility and personal task management.
The three board types are:
Action Board
Ask Boards
Project Boards
These boards are designed to work together. Asks and tasks can appear on their respective boards for strategic planning and also appear on the Action Board for personal follow through. This allows teams to manage projects and fundraising pipelines while each team member can track their daily responsibilities in one place.
Board Types at a Glance
Action Board
The Action Board is each team member’s personal home board. It shows nudges, assigned actions, tasks, and asks that the user is responsible for completing. The Action Board helps individuals manage their day-to-day work and ensures nothing slips through the cracks.
Use the Action Board to:
Act on nudges
Complete activities
Manage daily priorities
Ask Boards
Ask Boards are used to track fundraising Asks as they move through stages such as Identify, Cultivate, Solicit, and Close. Each Ask represents a planned solicitation or fundraising request tied to a contact. Ask Boards provide a visual way to manage donor relationships and forecast fundraising progress.
Use Ask Boards for:
Major gifts
Sponsorships
Grants
Planned giving
Membership invitations
Project Boards
Project Boards are designed to organize tasks into stages that reflect how work gets done. Each task belongs to one Project Board and can be moved across lanes as work progresses. Project Boards are ideal for managing campaigns, events, content planning, and internal projects.
Use Project Boards for:
Campaign planning
Event coordination
Grant writing workflows
Content calendars
Operational projects
Otto Tips
⚓
Let boards work together:
Tasks and Asks can live on their boards and still show up on the Action Board for individual accountability.
🌊
Keep your boards clean:
Update stages and complete items regularly so boards reflect real progress.
🗺️
Start your day at the Action Board:
Your Action Board is the fastest way to see what needs attention today.

articles.title: Customize Your Personal Board Settings and Notifications
articles.content:
Customize Your Personal Board Settings and Notifications
Each DonorDock team member can customize their board settings, including how nudges appear on the Action Board and which email notifications they receive. These settings let you control how and when you are prompted to take action, so DonorDock fits your workflow rather than interrupting it.
Personal board settings apply only to your user account. Administrators cannot set these preferences for you. Each team member must manage their own notification and nudge settings.
How Personal Board Settings Work
Your personal settings control:
Whether you receive email notifications when Board activities are assigned to you
Whether you receive email notifications when Otto creates new nudges or actions
Which nudges appear on your Action Board
Nudges are system-generated suggestions to engage with contacts. They are not actions themselves and do not create activity records until you convert them into a specific action. Nudges appear only on the Action Board and do not show on contact records or in activity reports until you take action on them.
Steps at a Glance
Open your profile settings
Review your email notification preferences
Customize which nudges you receive
Save your changes
Full Navigation Steps
Step 1: Open Your Personal Profile Settings
You can access your personal board settings in two ways:
Option A: From the Settings Menu
Click the
Settings menu
(grid icon in the top right of DonorDock)
Select
My Profile
Option B: From the Action Board
Open the
Action Board
Click
Customize
at the top of the board
Both options take you to your personal profile page, where you can update notification and nudge settings.
Step 2: Configure Email Notifications
On your profile page, you can toggle the following email notifications:
Send assigned activity email notification
Receive an email when an Action, Ask, or Project activity is assigned to you.
Send new action notification
Receive an email when Otto creates a new action or nudge for you.
These automated emails allow you to stay aware of new work and reminders directly from your email inbox, even when you are not logged into DonorDock. This helps keep track of changes and new assignments throughout the day.
Step 3: Customize Nudge Types
From your profile settings, you can choose which types of nudges appear on your Action Board. This lets you focus on the reminders and suggestions that are most relevant to your role.
Disabling nudge types you do not use helps reduce noise and keeps your Action Board focused
.
Step 4: Save Your Preferences
Once you have updated your notification and nudge settings, save your changes. Your Action Board will update to reflect your preferences.
Nudges
Nudges are system-generated suggestions to engage with contacts based on your data and engagement history. They are meant to prompt timely outreach, such as following up after a gift, reconnecting with a donor who has gone quiet, or acknowledging an important milestone.
Nudges are not actions themselves.
They do not create an activity record in DonorDock until you choose to act on them. When you convert a nudge into an action, you select the activity type, such as a phone call, email, task, or Ask, and that activity is then created and tracked like any other activity in DonorDock.
Nudges only appear on the Action Board. They do not show on contact records and are not included in activity reports until they are converted into a specific activity. This keeps nudges lightweight and focused on prompting action without cluttering activity history until real work begins.
Available Nudge Types
Nudge Name
Description
Daily 5
Generated suggestions that are created by the system if you have not engaged with a donor within 30 days or more. No more than five of these daily tasks will show in the suggestions on any given day.
First Gift Anniversary
Notification on the anniversary of the Donor's first gift
Major gifts
When setting up your organization's settings, you can define what constitutes a major gift. The default value is $1000.00, but you can configure this field to align with your organization's operating practices.
Spike-up gifts
A spike-up gift is one that is out of the ordinary for a donor. For example, if a donor's average gift is $50 and they then give a $350 donation, that would be a spike. A spike-up gift is a great opportunity to reach out to a donor and learn more about what drove them to give more than they normally do. Did something change with their personal circumstances? Did something your nonprofit did resonate with them? You can set the amount above their average gift that triggers the spike-up gift notification in your Settings. The default value is $100.00
First gifts
As the name suggests, this is a nudge to engage with a donor when they give their very first gift to your nonprofit. This deserves an individual engagement activity
Second gifts
Perhaps even more important to your organization than a first gift, the second gift is significant as it moves a donor from a one-time giver to a retained donor. This is a big deal and deserves an engagement touch-point from your organization. You will receive a nudge on the ActionBoard for every second gift
Reactivated donors
Donors that have moved from an archived to an activated status
Donor moving toward inactivity
The donor has not given a gift in at least 6 months, and has not had any interaction in at least 3 months
Donor birthdays
The birthday of the Donor
Pledge payment reminders
When a donor payment for the pledged amount is due
Contacts marked as deceased are automatically excluded from nudges.
Otto Tips
🧭
Tune your signal:
Turn off nudges that do not apply to your role so your Actions Board stays focused.
⚓
Let your inbox help:
Email notifications are handy when you are away from DonorDock but still need to stay on top of assignments.
🛟
Take the shortest route:
The Customize button on the Actions Board is the fastest way to adjust your personal settings.
🗺️
You’re the captain of your board:
Only you can change your personal board settings, so set them up to match how you work best.

articles.content:
Automation Journeys
Donor journeys are intentional, step-by-step engagement paths that help guide your donors through meaningful interactions with your organization. Using DonorDock, you can automate and personalize these journeys to strengthen donor relationships.
The Six Strategic Donor Segments

Recurring Donors

articles.title: Automation Triggers
articles.content:
Automation Triggers
Automation Triggers initiate a sequence of events within an Automation. These triggers are employed to initiate the specific actions defined for the Automation.
DonorDock offers the following Automation Triggers:
⚡Contact Created
⚡Contact Updated
⚡Contact Stage Changed
⚡Recurring Donor Created
⚡Contact Added to Badge
⚡Contact Added to Marketing List

⚡Gift Updated

You can apply additional filters once the trigger is set to specify when the Automation should run.

articles.title: Automation Steps
articles.content:
Automation Steps
Once a Trigger has been set on your Automation, you may set the Steps you would like to take after the triggering event. Automation may have multiple steps (up to 20). Activities set in subsequent steps will be created at the same as the Trigger, with the due date or send date being able to be set up to 365 days in the future.
Steps available
Send Email
Set an email to send to the contact, either from a prebuilt template or email content entered directly on the automation.
Send Internal Email
Set up an internal email to send the email addresses of your choice. Email addresses listed on this step do not need to be registered DonorDock team members.
Send Text
Set a text to send to the contact
Send Letter
Creates a new incomplete letter activity for completion. The step may be set to be completed by the contact's owner or a specified organization user. The incomplete activity will appear on the ActionBoard for completion for the activity owner. Letters may be set with a specific template or by typing a note or letter content into the automation.
Create Task
Creates a new incomplete Task activity for completion. The step may be set to be completed by the contact's owner or a specified organization user. The incomplete activity will appear on the ActionBoard for completion for the activity owner. Task notes may be added in the automation step
Add Badge
Add a badge to the contact after the triggering event
Add to Marketing List
Add a badge to the contact after the triggering event
Remove Badge
Remove a badge fro the contact after the triggering event
Remove from Marketing List
Remove a Marketing List from the contact after the triggering event
Schedule Meeting
Creates a new incomplete Meeting activity for completion. The step may be set to be completed by the contact's owner or a specified organization user. The incomplete activity will appear on the ActionBoard for completion for the activity owner. Meeting notes may be added in the automation step
Schedule Call
Creates a new incomplete Phone call activity for completion. The step may be set to be completed by the contact's owner or a specified organization user. The incomplete activity will appear on the ActionBoard for completion for the activity owner. Phone call notes may be added in the automation step
Call Webhook
Call webhook refers to triggering a request to a specific URL (webhook) to notify or communicate with another system or service.
Add ActionBoard Nudge
Add a customized ActionBoard nudge to the ActionBoad of the contact's owner for suggested interaction.
You can apply additional filters once a step has been set to specify when the Automation runs.
💡 Steps may also be rearranged in an automation by clicking and dragging a step card to a new position in the automation. Doing so will only change the position the card appeared in your automation and does not change any filter or date settings on the step.

articles.title: Viewing Available Outreach Emails
articles.content:
Viewing Available Outreach Emails
DonorDock classifies emails as either Marketing or Transactional.
Marketing emails
are used when sending bulk communications through the Outreach tool or individual emails created with the Send Email activity.
Transactional emails
are sent in response to donations, such as a receipt or an annual contribution statement. Transactional emails do not count towards your monthly email allotment.
Monthly Outreach (Marketing) Emails are based on your subscription level. If you need more, you can purchase add-ons for your DonorDock subscription. Monthly emails are used first, and additional ones roll over each month.
View Current Available Emails
Navigate to
Outreach
at the top of DonorDock
Select
Emails
Next to the header Bulk Emails, the number of emails currently available will be highlighted in blue
To view a breakdown of your available emails, click the question mark at the end of your available email count
A box will come up displaying the itemized email counts for the current month, including:
Monthly Email: the base amount of emails given by your subscription
Sent Emails: the total amount of emails already sent this month
Additional Emails: Additional emails purchased in addition to your subscription emails
Scheduled Emails: Emails that have been created and are scheduled to be sent at a later point
Available Emails: Sum total of available emails to send
🙋🏽‍♀️
Do dropped emails count against my monthly email limit?
Yes, Dropped emails continue to be counted in your monthly email quota. These emails are not labeled as dropped until after an initial attempt to send them, at which point we receive feedback from the email server that the email sent could not be completed due to a previous bounce. Consequently, dropped emails will still be considered part of your monthly plan's email allocation.
🙋🏼‍♂️
Can I delete dropped emails in bulk from contact records?
Currently, there is not a way to bulk delete emails (or other select information from contacts); however, what you can do is create a new marketing list based on the last send.
Navigate to Outreach > Emails > Sent Emails
Click to view the most recent sent email
Once on the email summary page, you may click to view the group email report
Scroll over on the right to the column for
dropped
emails and click the filter icon (looks like a funnel)
Select to filter all activities that are False for the
dropped
value. This will filter out all
dropped
contacts on the report
Click the Add button at the top of the report to add the remaining contacts to a new, updated marketing list
Once all contacts have been added to the new list, you may delete the old list by navigating to
Contacts
>
Contact Lists
and clicking the trash can icon next to the old list. This will remove the Marketing List from all contacts tagged on the list.

articles.title: Sending Individual Emails
articles.content:
Sending Individual Emails through DonorDock
While you will likely send emails in batches, you can also create individual emails and send individual contacts by creating a "Send Email" activity for the contact.
When creating the "Send Email" activity in DonorDock, you are actively sending the email at the time you create the activity.
If you wish to log an email already sent, this would be completed using the "Log Email" activity option.
Fields to select when creating a Send Email Activity:
Send to.
The contact that you are sending the email to. The email will be send to the contact's primary email address.
Send from.
The sender will default to you as the one creating the activity. If you need the email to be from a different user from your organization, you may select a different user.
Email Subject.
The subject of the email as it will appear on the contact's activity timeline and the email subject seen by the contact.
Use Template
(toggle). If using a template, you will click the toggle to turn on and the Email Message field will disappear and instead you will be asked to select the template you wish to send. The only Templates that can be used for this activity are Marketing Templates. Transactional templates would be sent as receipts.
Email Message.
If not using a Template, here is where you can type the body of the email you are sending to your contact. Simple text formatting options will be available for use at the top of the message box.
Campaign.
Campaign (if any) the email activity is associated with.
Appeal.
Appeal (if any) the email activity is associated with.
Can I send an Image or Attachment in a One-off Email from DonorDock?
No, this is not functionality that in DonorDock as attachments greatly impact the deliverability of the email and increase the odds that the email will be flagged as spam by the recipient.
However, you can create a personal email from your inbox with the content, images, etc. that you wish and track the email activity back to a contact's record in DonorDock.

articles.title: Text-to-Donate Overview

Text-to-Donate

This keyword may be used at events, shared via email, or included in direct mail to make donating to your organization as easy as possible.

articles.title: Text Conversations Overview
articles.content:
Text Conversations 💬
It is estimated that over
7 billion people worldwide
will have smartphones by 2024, with over 60% of people reading their text messages within 1 to 5 minutes of receipt. This makes Texting a popular and convenient form of outreach for nonprofits.
Texting features in DonorDock allow for bulk text message communications and individual text conversations with your contacts that will show a running history of your text communications with a contact.
⚠️ To send and receive text messages through DonorDock, you must complete
A2P 10DLC registration
to comply with current laws and regulations.
To Access Text Conversations
Navigate to
Outreach
at the top of your DonorDock
Select
Texting
From the submenu options, select
Conversations
The Text Conversations page is divided into three sections of information.
Conversation Inbox
On the left side of the page, an inbox list of open conversations will appear in descending order of recent message date. Selecting a contact row from the inbox will show their text conversation string on the Conversation Panel in the center. By default, visiting the Text Conversations page will open the most recently active conversation.
💡 A filter is available at the top of the inbox to select if you wish to switch the view from the Open conversations Inbox to closed conversations or blocked conversations. A conversation may be closed on the conversation panel if you are no longer actively interacting with the contact to keep your inbox streamlined. Any response or message from a contact will re-open their conversation. A conversation will show blocked contacts if you have blocked any contacts (for example, if receiving a spam message).
Conversation Panel
The Text Conversation Panel is located in the center of the Text Conversations page. Here, you may view text messages sent from and to the contact and type and send a response. Texts from the contact will appear in gray text bubbles on the left, while conversations from your organization will appear in blue text bubbles on the right.
The conversation history will show all text messages sent and received, either individually, as part of a bulk text send, or through auto-response features such as Text-to-Donate. Messages sent from your organization's phone number will show the team member's name who sent the text. If a text response were automated, such as a Text-to-Donate response or an automated response for unsubscribing, the sender would show as "auto-response".
💡 If a text message fails to be delivered for any reason, such as a bad phone number or insufficient text credits, a message in red will show on the text.
Contact Summary Card
A card showing a summary of contact information will be available on the right for the contact conversation that is currently selected. This summary will show the contact's name, phone number, Contact badges, and other basic contact information.
The action icon on the card (3 vertical dots) may be clicked to select the actions to view the contact record, edit the contact record, or block the contact. If a contact is blocked, their conversation will automatically be moved from the Open conversation inbox into the Blocked conversations inbox. If you need to unblock a contact, you may navigate to the blocked conversation inbox and click the link to unblock the contact.

articles.title: Understanding Text Credits in DonorDock
articles.content:
Understanding Text Credits in DonorDock
Text Credits
are used to send and receive messages in DonorDock.
A base number of Text Credits are allotted to your organization monthly for outreach purposes, depending on your organization's subscription level.
💡 Additional Text Credits do not expire once purchased, and additional text credits may be purchased anytime. When texts are sent through DonorDock, Monthly Texts are used first before using any additional texts available on the account.
The length of the text message determines the cost of each text message sent and received in DonorDock. Generally, text messages of up to 160 characters use 1 Text Credit, and messages of 161-320 characters use 2 Text Credits.
💡Including emojis or special characters in your text messages can impact the number of Text Credits used in DonorDock. Standard SMS messages support up to 160 characters per Text Credit. However, if a message contains even one emoji or special Unicode character, the limit drops to 70 characters per Text Credit. This means messages with emojis may use more credits than expected, as they are calculated in smaller segments. Keep this in mind when composing messages to optimize your text credit usage.
When setting up
Text-to-Donate
keywords on Online Giving pages, you will see an estimated credit calculation for how many text credits are expected to be used for each Text-to-Donate exchange (generally 2-3 based on the text-to-donate response message).
When sending
individual text messages
through the Text Conversations inbox or when creating a new Sent Text activity, the estimated text credit cost will appear at the bottom of the message box.
When sending
outreach text messages
through bulk texting, the calculation of text messages will appear at the bottom of the message box, showing how many text credits are estimated to be used per recipient, as well as in total.
🙋🏻‍♀️ What happens if I run out of Text Message Credits?

articles.title: A2P 10 DLC Registration Information
articles.content:
A2P 10DLC Registration
A2P 10DLC
is an acronym for "Application-to-Person 10 Digit Long Code." This refers to using an application (such as DonorDock) to send and receive text and muli-media messages with a 10-digit phone number.
This is a mandatory registration to be compliant with current laws and regulations
The purpose of 10 DLC registration is to reduce spam and fraudulent messaging, enhance message deliverability, and provide a more secure and trusted environment for A2P messaging. Registration also helps establish trust and credibility with your donors. When a message comes from a registered long code, it is more likely to be seen as legitimate, which is particularly important for nonprofits seeking to build trust.
We have worked diligently to make this registration process as simple and transparent as possible while adhering to all regulations.

articles.title: Tasks
articles.content:
Tasks
Task activities in DonorDock are a specific activity type designed to track work that needs to be planned or completed. Unlike other activity types such as phone calls, emails, letters, or texts, Tasks are meant to represent actionable to-do items rather than communication events. A task might be something like preparing event materials, reviewing a grant draft, building a report, or following up on a process step.
Tasks can be linked to Project Boards and appear on a user’s Actions Board, making them the primary activity type for organizing and managing work across projects. Each task can belong to one Project Board at a time for project-level visibility, while also showing on the Actions Board for individual accountability. This allows teams to see both how work fits into a larger project and who is responsible for completing each step.
Because tasks are distinct activity types, they complement other activities rather than replace them. For example, a task might remind someone to make a phone call, while the phone call itself is logged as a separate activity. This separation helps teams clearly track both the work to be done and the interactions with contacts, keeping project management and donor engagement organized and easy to follow.

articles.title: Asks
articles.content:
Asks
Ask activities in DonorDock are used to plan, track, and manage fundraising requests as part of a structured moves management process. Each Ask represents a specific solicitation or fundraising action tied to a contact, such as a major gift request, sponsorship ask, or grant proposal. By tracking Asks separately from gifts, teams can focus on relationship-building steps and ensure outreach efforts are intentional and well timed.
Asks move through defined Ask Stages that reflect the current status of the relationship and the likelihood of success. When using the AskBoard, these stages appear as lanes on a visual board, making it easy to see where each Ask stands, prioritize next steps, and coordinate work across team members. Asks can be created individually or in bulk, assigned to owners, and updated as conversations progress.
Completing an Ask signals that the solicitation has reached an outcome, whether a commitment was made, declined, or deferred. Asks track the fundraising activity itself, not the receipt of funds, allowing teams to maintain accurate pipelines and reporting. This approach helps organizations stay organized, forecast more effectively, and build stronger donor relationships over time.

DonorDock + Zapier Overview
Your DonorDock account has the ability to connect with Zapier, a tool that links thousands of cloud apps and services. Zapier gives your organization advanced flexibility and coordination between tools, making it easier to connect DonorDock with the platforms you rely on, such as event management, form builders, accounting systems, calendars, and more.
💡Zapier offers both free and paid plans, so you can choose the option that best fits your needs. Your Zapier subscription is separate from your DonorDock subscription and is maintained independently.
🔨⚙️ How Zapier Works
Zapier acts as a bridge between DonorDock and the other tools your organization uses, especially when there isn’t a direct integration already built in. By creating automated workflows called
Zaps
, Zapier lets your apps “talk” to each other without manual effort.
Each Zap connects at least two applications: one providing the
trigger
(the event that starts the workflow) and the other carrying out the
action
(the task that follows).
For example:
When someone submits a form through Typeform (trigger), a new contact can be created in DonorDock (action).
When a transaction is processed in Square (trigger), a new gift record can be created in DonorDock (action).
This flexibility allows you to tailor workflows to your specific needs, reduce manual entry, and keep your data coordinated across all your tools.
Quick Overview Steps
Create a
Zapier account
(free or paid, depending on your needs).
Connect DonorDock and your other tools to Zapier.
Build your first
Zap
by choosing:
A
Trigger
(the event that starts the workflow, like a form submission).
An
Action
(what happens next, like creating a contact or gift in DonorDock).
Test your Zap to make sure it works.
Turn it on and let Zapier handle the automation.
Understanding Triggers and Actions
Zapier runs on the concept of
Triggers
and
Actions
:
Triggers
: An event that starts the workflow.
Example: A supporter submits a form on your website.
Example: A payment is processed in Square.
Actions
: The task that happens as a result of the trigger.
Example: A new contact is created in DonorDock.
Example: A new gift record is created in DonorDock.
A trigger in an outside app can create an action in DonorDock, and a trigger in DonorDock can create an action in another app.
Otto Tips
🌊
Start small:
Begin with a simple Zap like “form submission → new contact” before building more advanced workflows.
🦑
Automate the repetitive:
Look for tasks you do over and over; those are the best candidates for Zapier.
🌊
Two ships, two crews:
Your DonorDock subscription and your Zapier subscription sail separately. While DonorDock supports the Zapier Connector, we do not support individual Zaps, Zap setup, or other Zapier-connected services.
